title: Elevator schema in PostgreSQL
idea: The elevator schema stores floors, cars and hall calls so PostgreSQL enforces the rules: one open call per button, real floors only, legal states only.

analogy.text: A hotel desk with one key hook per room. A second key cannot hang on a taken hook until the first one comes back.
analogy.breaks: A served call frees its hook, but its row stays for history.

points: A composite foreign key to `floor` rejects calls and cars on missing floors.
A partial unique index allows one PENDING or ASSIGNED call per button.
A partial index on `elevator_id` serves a car's open calls and failover.
Assign locks the call `FOR UPDATE`; a `version` column guards car state.

steps.caption: Two panels on floor 5 send UP at the same moment.
Panel A inserts first. The partial unique index now holds one open 5 UP call.
Panel B's insert hits the index. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` skips it, and B reads the open call.
The call is locked `FOR UPDATE`, matched to the nearest car in service, and marked ASSIGNED.
The operator takes E2 out of service with version 1. The row moves to version 2.
The controller still holds version 1. Its update matches zero rows: a stale write is refused.
Failover moves E2's open call back to PENDING and assigns it to E1.

code.title: Tables and constraints
code.caption: The schema on a real PostgreSQL 18, then bad writes that the database refuses by itself.

walk.text: Every floor is a row, so a foreign key can check any floor number.
elevator: state is TEXT with a CHECK, plus a version and a real floor.
hall_call: checked direction and status, and a named check that assigned calls have a car.
Partial unique index: at most one open call per floor and button.
Partial index for listing a car's open calls during dispatch and failover.
Each bad write prints the Postgres error code and the constraint that stopped it.
Once the call is SERVED, the same button can open a new call.

code.title: Press, assign, fail over
code.caption: Parallel presses and parallel dispatchers, then optimistic locking and failover. It uses trimmed tables so the races stay short.

walk.text: A press inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, else returns the open call's id.
Assign locks the PENDING call FOR UPDATE, then picks the nearest car in service.
Mark the call ASSIGNED and commit; any error rolls the transaction back.
Two presses and two dispatchers run in parallel; print counts, never who won.
Optimistic locking: a write that still carries version 1 updates zero rows.
Failover: E2's open calls go back to PENDING and are assigned again.

pitfalls: Without the partial index, two panels can open two calls for one button.
Never update car state without the `version` check; stale writes silently win.
Keep `WHERE status = 'PENDING'` in the locking SELECT, or both dispatchers assign.

quiz.q: What does assign.mjs print for the two parallel dispatchers?
quiz.why: The second dispatcher waits on the row lock. After the first commits, the row is ASSIGNED, so its PENDING filter matches nothing.

takeaway: Let indexes, foreign keys and row locks enforce the dispatch rules.

starters: Why a partial unique index instead of a plain UNIQUE constraint?
Should car calls be stored in the database too?
When would pessimistic locking on the elevator row be better than a version column?
